label: sparse, early-sequence conjunction: digit-first prefix with u/t/p (no clean rule)
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.04% of steps) whose activations sit early in the sequence: original steps t=3-5 and copy steps with recall_idx 2-3, more often in short sequences (L=3-4). Many top examples share a prefix that starts with a digit (2 or 0) followed by u/t/p, e.g. 2 0 u t [i], 0 t u [s], 2 u p [3]. Copy-phase activations favour inputs i/a/c/j/3/2 with outputs 2/t/0, but every per-token rule has precision below 1%. The best predicate, original phase t=3-5 with the first token 0/2 and at least two of u/t/p seen, reaches only about 11% precision and 10% recall on dev. Activation looks like a narrow region of the hidden state reached by specific prefix combinations, not a single readable variable. It is essentially silent at t=0-1, at the delimiter, and after the copy goes wrong. No magnitude trend was established.
